sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number 2235.54.7)
sources.note: Nothing. The 'Alphabet' section (pp.17-19) gives letter values only and passes straight to 'De l'article'; the words 'accent'/'tonique' occur nowhere in the book. Only prosodic remark (p.46): the final vowel of the conditional suffixes -yà, -gà, -gayà, -genyà 'est long, traîné, chanté. L'intonation est caractéristique.'

sources.citation: Awagana, Ari & Camille Lefebvre. 2025. L'œuvre en kanouri d'al-Hajj Musa ibn Hissein, un savant du Borno (Niger-Nigéria). Leiden: Brill (open access).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Texts are Manga/Yerwa Kanuri, not Bilma-Mowar. Fig. 2 places Bilma+Fachi under a 'Kawar' node and Mowar under 'Est'. p.93 translates Prietze's early-1900s remark that in Kanuri 'l'accent tonique.. ne se manifeste pas de la même manière que dans les langues européennes' — about Manga, second-hand, not usable for bms.

sources.citation: Bulakarima, Shettima Umara. 1996. Kanembu-Kanuri relationship: a proposal. Berichte des Sonderforschungsbereichs 268, Bd. 8: 37-49. Frankfurt a.M.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No prose statement on tone or stress. Appendix (pp.45-49) gives a fully tone-marked comparative wordlist with separate Bilma and Mowar columns (e.g. Bilma cúró 'belly', shîm 'eye', kùngúsù 'louse'), i.e. the varieties are treated as lexically tonal like the rest of Kanuri. Cites Bulakarima 1991 Unimaid PhD 'A Study in Kanuri Dialectology: Phonology and Dialectal Distribution in Mowar' (= the 2001 book).

sources.citation: Peace Corps Niger. 1993. Manuel de Kanuri (Kanuri Manual). Niamey. ERIC ED401747, 89 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Checked pp.1-10 (scanned) for a dialect or pronunciation note: none; lessons start directly with vocabulary that looks Manga (fado 'house'). Not a Bilma-Mowar source; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Jarrett, Kevin A. 1988. Dialectes et alphabétisation dans les écoles: une étude explorative de l'intercompréhension des différents dialectes kanuri du Niger. Journal of West African Languages 18(2): 105-124.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. pp.106-107 classify Niger Kanuri dialects (Mobar+Bilma = one eastern sub-group, the basis of Glottolog's bilm1238); p.108 only a generic remark that many African languages are tonal and tone is not written in the orthography. Comparative word/affix tables and text samples for Bilma and Mobar are untoned.
